*************************************************** RESONANCE REGION Authors: G.P.A. Nobre, A. Palumbo, M. Herman
Artificial resonances generated by EMPIRE
*************************************************** FAST ENERGY REGION Authors: G.P.A. Nobre, A. Palumbo, M. Chadwick, M. Herman
EMPIRE code was used to describe fast neutron region. Due to the lack of data in the fast region available for this isotope, the EMPIRE parameters were taken from the 169Tm evaluation. The (n,2n) and (n,g) cross sections above the resonance region were replaced by the LANL radchem evaluation.
CROSS-SECTION EVALUATION PROCEDURE
Adopted procedure is based on careful theoretical analysis utilizing available experimental data and nuclear reaction model calculations.
Available experimental data were interpreted using nuclear reaction model code EMPIRE-3 by M. Herman et al [EMP]. This code integrates into a single system a number of important modules and features:
- Spherical and deformed Optical Model including coupled-channels (ECIS06 by J. Raynal) - Hauser-Feshbach statistical model including HRTW width fluctuation correction - Quantum-mechanical MSD TUL model (codes ORION & TRISTAN by H. Lenske), and MSC NVWY model - Exciton model with angular momentum coupling (code DEGAS by E. Betak and P. Oblozinsky) that represents a good approximation to the DSD model - Exciton model with Iwamoto-Harada cluster emission and Kalbach systematic angular distr. (code PCROSS by R.Capote et al) - Complete gamma-ray cascade after emission of each particle, including realistic treatment of discrete transitions - Access to OM segment of the RIPL library [RIPL] - Built-in input parameter files, such as masses, level density, discrete levels, fission barriers and gamma strength functions based on the RIPL library [RIPL] - Automatic retrieval of experimental data from the EXFOR/CSISRS library - ENDF-6 formatting (code EMPEND by A. Trkov) coupled to graphical presentation capabilities (code ZVView by V. Zerkin) through the chain of PrePro codes by R. Cullen - Checking codes (CHECKR, FIZCON, PSYCHE) - Support for NJOY
PARAMETERIZATIONS
Following models and parameters were used in the current evaluation:
Discrete levels were taken from the RIPL-3 level file, based on the 2007 version of ENSDF. EMPIRE-specific level densities Width fluctuations calculated within HRTW up to 1.00 MeV ENDF formatting enabled Exclusive spectra available up to emission loop # 2 Exciton model calculations with code PCROSS Cluster emission in terms of the Iwamoto-Harada model Kalbach systematics angular distributions (see RIPL-1) Mean free path parameter in PCROSS set to 1.5 (Recommended ~ 1.5 Coupled Channels (ECIS) used for direct inelastic scattering For all nuclei: fission ignored All response functions in MSD normalized by factor 1.050 Imag. surface potential radius in 169Tm scaled by 1.08 Volume real potential radius in 169Tm scaled by 0.94 Imag. volume potential radius in 169Tm scaled by 1.06 Real volume potential depth in 169Tm scaled by 1.03 Imag. surface potential depth in 169Tm scaled by 1.05 Imag. volume potential depth in 169Tm scaled by 1.05 Imag. surface potential diff. in 169Tm scaled by 1.06 Volume potential diffuseness in 169Tm scaled by 1.00 Fusion cross section was scaled by factor 0.920 Total cross section was scaled by factor 0.956 All response functions in MSD normalized by factor 1.758 E1 strength function set to MLO1 GDR parameters from RIPL-2/Exp.data+Plujko systematics
